To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) newspaper coverage of a company depends positively on the amount of ads that a given company purchases on a given newspaper; (2) coverage is higher after the publication of a press release; (3) this effect is stronger on newspapers where more advertising is purchased; (4) coverage is correlated with stock market performance; and (5) this effect is steeper on newspapers where more advertisements are purchased.

the amount of ads a given company purchases on a given newspaper is positively related to the amount of coverage that newspaper gives to that company, and that this relationship is particularly pronounced for press releases and for those newspapers where a given company purchases more ads.

(i) newspaper coverage of a listed company is positively related to the amount of advertising that company has purchased on that newspaper and (ii) newspaper coverage of listed companies is higher the day following the release of a company press release, but this relationship is steeper for newspapers where more ads have been purchased by the company.

the amount of advertising that companies buy in the press affects both the amount and the quality of the coverage they receive.
